Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments carefully.

nda-11: No reverse engineering — The document doesn't mention reverse engineering anywhere. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-16: Return of confidential information — The document doesn't mention returning or destroying confidential information upon termination. Segment [14] says layout plans stay in Discloser's custody, but this isn't about return upon termination. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-15: No licensing — The document doesn't explicitly state that the Agreement grants no rights/license to Confidential Information. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement — The document doesn't say the fact of the Agreement itself is confidential. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information — Segment [3] says Confidential Information includes "security set-up, security architecture, lay-out, security processes and procedures, designs, drawings, software and hardware configuration, computer programs, algorithms, services, customers etc". This includes non-technical information like "services, customers". So this contradicts the hypothesis that CI shall ONLY include technical information. Label: Contradiction, evidence [3].

nda-1: Explicit identification — Segment [7] says "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing". This suggests CI is "identified" — the hypothesis says "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." Segment [7] says the information is "identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing at the time of such disclosure." This does indicate identification at time of disclosure. Hmm, this is a standard "Explicit identification" clause. The text says Confidential Information "as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing at the time of such disclosure of the information." This suggests all CI is identified at disclosure time. I'd lean toward Entailment with evidence [7].

nda-19: Survival of obligations — The document doesn't mention survival of obligations after termination. Segment [29] talks about term continuing until termination. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-12: Permissible development of similar information — Not mentioned. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession — Not mentioned. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information — Segment [7] says CI can be "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." Also segment [3] lists types of CI. So CI may include verbally conveyed information. Label: Entailment, evidence [7].

nda-18: No solicitation — Not mentioned. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-7: Sharing with third-parties — Segment [10] says Recipient agrees not to share with any Third Party. This contradicts "may share with third-parties." Label: Contradiction, evidence [10].

nda-17: Permissible copy — Not mentioned explicitly. Segment [15] says Recipient has access to layout plan for installation purposes, but not copying. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure — Segment [11] says Recipient agrees to use best efforts to prevent disclosure "even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser." This means if required by law, Recipient needs Discloser's permission — which implies notification/consent. Hmm, "without the express permission of the Discloser" — this is close to requiring notice/consent for compelled disclosure. The hypothesis says "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose." The clause requires express permission, which is stronger than notice. This could be Entailment — requiring permission implies the Discloser must be informed. I'd say Entailment with evidence [11].

nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information — Not mentioned. Label: NotMentioned.

nda-5: Sharing with employees — Segment [10] says no sharing with any Third Party; segment [11] says prevent disclosure to "any person(s) or entity(ies)". Employees aren't addressed. Standard labeling: NotMentioned. Actually, [11] says disclosure to any person without express permission — this would suggest even employees can't be shared with without permission, which might contradict "may share with employees." But typically in these tasks, if employees aren't mentioned, it's NotMentioned. The clause says prevent disclosure to any person(s) without express permission of Discloser — with permission, sharing is allowed. Hmm. The hypothesis is "Receiving Party may share some CI with some of Receiving Party's employees." The document doesn't specifically address employees. I'll say NotMentioned.

nda-4: Limited use — Segment [5] defines Purpose (supply, installation, testing and commissioning of CCTV System). Segment [10] says "Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" — actually it says not to use in any way or share with Third Party. Segment [15] says access to layout plan for purpose of carrying out the contract. The limited use hypothesis: "shall not use any CI for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Segment [10] "No Use: Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" combined with [5] purpose. Evidence: [5], [10]. Label: Entailment.
